title: Merge Sorted Feeds

statement.md: A consolidated tape merges $k$ venue feeds. Each feed is already sorted in ascending order. Merge them into one ascending sequence and print it on a single line, separated by single spaces. If there are no values at all, print an empty line.

inputFormat: First line: $k$. Then $k$ lines, each `m x_1 ... x_m`: the length of the feed followed by its values (a feed may be empty, `0`).
outputFormat: One line with all values in ascending order.
hints: Concatenating and sorting costs $O(N \log N)$ and ignores that the feeds are sorted. What does a heap of size $k$ give you?
Keep one cursor per feed, and a min-heap of the current head of each non-empty feed.
editorial: [{"type": "p", "md": "Push the first value of each non-empty feed into a min-heap together with the feed index and position. Repeatedly pop the smallest, append it, and push the next value from the same feed. The heap never holds more than $k$ entries, so the time is $O(N \\log k)$. Ties may come out in any order because equal values are identical in the output."}]

import sys


def merge_lists(k, lists):
    """Each list is sorted ascending. Return one line: all values merged in ascending order, separated by single spaces (an empty line if there are none)."""

solutions.python:
import heapq
import sys


def main():
    tok = sys.stdin.read().split()
    k = int(tok[0])
    pos = 1
    feeds = []
    for _ in range(k):
        m = int(tok[pos])
        feeds.append(tok[pos + 1:pos + 1 + m])
        pos += 1 + m
    heap = [(int(f[0]), i, 0) for i, f in enumerate(feeds) if f]
    heapq.heapify(heap)
    out = []
    while heap:
        v, i, j = heapq.heappop(heap)
        out.append(str(v))
        if j + 1 < len(feeds[i]):
            heapq.heappush(heap, (int(feeds[i][j + 1]), i, j + 1))
    print(' '.join(out))


main()
